artifacts.summary: 8-phase plan (5 dependency waves, 10h) for the hook-registration orphan sweep: one shared identity definition consumed by merge.lua and the hook-path lint, the sweep function, manager.load call-siting with two fail-safe gates, real-deploy before/after measurement, boundary-narrative invariant, and the full gate set.

memory_candidates.content: When reconciling a notion that two consumers in DIFFERENT LANGUAGES must share in this repo (e.g. merge.lua's hook_identity vs a bash lint's normalize_identity), the workable single-definition shape is: put the normative implementation in the side that cannot shell out (Lua, because merge.lua runs in-editor at extension load time), add a logic-free `nvim --headless --noplugin -u NONE -l` stdin/stdout bridge for the bash side invoked ONCE per run, make a bridge failure fatal rather than a silent fallback to a second notion, and retain a shared JSON fixture corpus as the conformance pin (a test, not the definition). The bridge is only ever needed in a repository that has source-store scan surfaces, which is the same repository that holds the Lua module -- that invariant is what makes the dependency safe.
